candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — child injury prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Teach evidence-based household injury-prevention measures for young children.

options.A: Lock medicines and household cleaners out of reach, anchor unstable furniture, maintain working smoke alarms, and use appropriate outlet protection.
options.B: Store medicines on a low open shelf so the child can identify them.
options.C: Leave heavy furniture unsecured because tip-over injuries occur only in adults.
options.D: Disable smoke alarms to prevent false alarms at night.

candidate.rationale: CPSC child-safety guidance recommends securing medicines and household chemicals, anchoring furniture and televisions to reduce tip-over risk, maintaining smoke alarms, and using electrical outlet safeguards for young children.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Childproofing includes secure storage of medicines/cleaners, furniture anchoring, smoke alarms, and electrical outlet protection.
